entries.title: Clearer workout records, swim timing and linked watch data
changes: Choose calories/kcal per minute or joules/watts in Settings; quiet equivalent readings retain clear metabolic-versus-mechanical labels and uncertainty ranges.
Watch imports can be linked to scheduled sessions or added as new workouts on their recorded date. Bike and watch recordings combine once, with a clock-adjustment preview and recorded metric sources.
Consistent workout cards and reports for swimming, cycling, strength, running, walking and other activities. Daily Hooper recovery stays separate; saved session reports collapse across views.
Workout library hearts start red for saved entries. Most recent performance cards, persistent comparison metrics, card navigation and repeat-click close controls make history easier to browse.
Plain-text strength editing preserves warm-up, main work and cool-down, optional planned/reported effort, set corrections and clearly labeled output estimates. Missing readings stay unknown.

Swim builder accepts goal-to-expected completion times: 400 FS 6 to 8 minutes. Watch lengths/laps compare by distance and order; consecutive drills stay combined unless you optionally report individual drill times. Timing drafts require three comparable performances and review.
Cancelled and missed workouts keep their sport icon and red cross. A finished day with no recorded work shows a separate checked recovery moon. Completion and plan revisions are tracked separately.
Phone ride controls are clearer, personal audio/video share a private local library, outlook flags are easier to scan, and incomplete route history no longer blocks ghost lookup.
Plan workout details use the same View/Hide control across sports and remain inside Plan, including today’s swims.

Swim Plan cards show a sectioned workout, stroke-distance donut and the existing front/back body heat map with a concise five-color key. Stroke-distance history offers 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 60 and 90 days, grouped by session or day. Distance, duration, average HR and descriptive HR × minutes stay separate; missing readings remain unknown.

Fitness Dashboard adds full-size swim history, custom dates and 1–12-month presets. Compare month, quarter, saved training phase or custom month groups using up to twelve body-map donuts, three per page or all together. Plan retains the compact 90-day history; Today stays unchanged.

entries.title: Shared workout recording tools
changes: 114 published tools, including watch-link review, completed workout library saves and optional swim drill split reports. Use with App 1.10.0.

entries.title: Recorded work, validated check-ins and a plan that watches its load
changes: Training energy now comes from the least heart-rate-dependent source: bike power, running and walking from distance, gradient and body mass (1 kcal per kg per km on the flat), and the watch for swims. The watch's number is shown beside it and large gaps are flagged.

Each check-in and workout report keeps the 3-day rate, biggest day and 28-day load it was made in, so later formula changes never move your history. Older reports can be rebuilt once through a preview.

Validated check-in questions: the Hooper questionnaire (fatigue, sleep, stress, soreness, 1–7), pain by site (0–10, kept apart from soreness), session effort on the CR-10 scale and the weekly OSTRC injury questionnaire.

Plan load outlook: your recorded and planned 3-day rate, biggest day and 28-day load against the phase's target, with report-gated running steps (3–10%) and sessions that went well in the last 90 days.

After a bad report (pain 5+, pain getting worse, soreness well above usual) the Hub holds running and asks a short re-check that evening and the next morning before deciding to resume, stay reduced or step back.

Body workload: an Overall ring of every region, group views with magnifying graphs, bars stacked by source and 28-day carried totals. Also: completed-workout reports, actual strength and swim logging, and a more responsive ride screen.

entries.title: Your music library and clearer workout records
changes: Added a private music folder library with songs, albums, artists, cover art and available tempo estimates. macOS has a native folder picker; other systems can use files from their browser.
Unified cycling creation in the typed workout builder, including watt ranges, cadence ranges, time targets and reusable starter rides.
Recorded and partial workouts show actual time separately from planned time; imported activity totals remain visible without a matching prescription.
Fixed music setup refresh and idle video timing; unavailable integrations are explicitly marked in progress.
Added browser and home-screen app icons and corrected the Windows credential-permissions test.

entries.title: A run-walk test for coming back to running
changes: At 60% of a running hold, a three-day test: a short run-walk, then how walking feels the next day, then stairs. A good result offers to start winding the hold down; anything else tries again in a week.
End on the ride screen now ends the whole ride: the workout and the route together.
The Hub now tells you when an update is out (checked at most twice a day; you can turn it off here).
Personal music folders and files from this device are available. Video playback no longer builds up in memory.

entries.title: The run-walk test for your assistant
changes: Added run_walk_test: your assistant can walk you through the three days and record each answer.
Assistant instructions match the new test and the End-ride behaviour.

entries.title: Morning inspiration and a visible update history
changes: Gave the morning diagnostic its own mountain-sunrise artwork.
Added this local update history with links to release details and the wiki.

entries.title: Clearer workouts and reliable reports
changes: Fixed effort reports for completed lifts without watch imports.
Added illustrated test guides and separate workout instructions and planning explanations.
Check-ins review explanations and update only what needs changing.

entries.title: Count the lift you actually performed
changes: Added pauses, weighted holds and failure reports to the lifting tools.
Aligned assistant instructions with the current hold calculation.

entries.title: A more complete coaching routine
changes: Added check-in attention lists and recorded race predictions.
Exposed current calibration, cross-sport rules and structured lifting through the assistant.

entries.title: Review the whole sequence
changes: Added a two-week running and lifting outlook.
Preview and approve calendar repairs and evidence-supported capacity changes.

entries.title: Guided setup and progression
changes: Added guided bike setup and recent-week review.
Expanded phase-specific starter progression and the simulated athlete journey.

entries.title: Apply the plan you reviewed
changes: Locked program changes to an exact reviewed draft.
Added calendar evidence, formula inspection and swim equipment including fins and snorkels.

entries.title: Smaller, more usable planning context
changes: Made program previews easier for assistants to read.
Verified the desktop extension installation and planning workflow.

entries.title: Build and compare programs
changes: Added program preview, apply and progress evidence.
Compare three proposed workloads before choosing a starter program.

entries.title: Bring lifting into the Hub
changes: Added lifting prescriptions, logs, follow-ups and Sunday reviews.

entries.title: Connect an assistant
changes: Published the first one-file MCP bundle for coaching, rides, imports and training load.

entries.title: The first public release
changes: The repository began its public history as a stationary-bike training hub.
During the following week it grew into a shared place for coaching, multisport load, recovery and program planning.

in_the_works.title: Forecasts from your own reports
in_the_works.detail: Fitting how your reports follow your recent rate and carried load, then predicting a planned week, with an accuracy scoreboard against what you actually report.

in_the_works.title: Learning your recovery curve
in_the_works.detail: Paused for a research review: recovery timing learned from your reports instead of starting values.

in_the_works.title: Lifting built on joints and movement directions
in_the_works.detail: Three full-body sessions (A, B, C) covering every joint action and direction, repeated and progressed for 4-6 weeks.

in_the_works.title: Likes, dislikes and learned rules
in_the_works.detail: Thumbs up or down on exercises after a workout; exercises you keep skipping come up less.

in_the_works.title: Personal music and video library
in_the_works.detail: Testing browser-playable formats and playback. Planned: random selections of 16 feature films and 32 music videos, with browsing by genre, director and participating artists as metadata becomes available.
